newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $64.00/passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $64.00/passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were inactive near midday Tuesday, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Light packer bids at $64.00 per cwt were passed by owners who were pricing cattle mostly at $66.00-$67.00, with a few at $68.00, the sources said.
Last sales were last week at $65.00 in active trading.

Sales this week were not expected until Wednesday or Thursday and were seen at prices steady to firm compared with last week's amid ideas several packers need cattle by the end of the week, sources said.

Further strength was expected on last Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, which showed a smaller-than-perceived movement of cattle into large feedlots in the seven primary cattle feeding states during December.
Support, however, was muted by concern that beef prices would continue to weaken despite relatively brisk sales, sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.09 to $1.09 per cwt on 193 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
